% \textsurd (√) in other fonts whose tex4ht files give a middle dot:
% pxfonts, whose file takes the Latin Modern TS1 one, loaded without
% textcomp and in OT1, txfonts, which has a file of its own, and TeX Gyre;
% and in Palladio (where LaTeX takes the sign from Computer Modern) and
% Computer Modern, chosen by family. \textperiodcentered stays a middle dot.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{pxfonts}
\begin{document}
Palatino \textsurd{} sign.
Pxdot \textperiodcentered{} sign.
\textit{Palitalic \textsurd{} sign.}
\textsf{Pxsans \textsurd{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{txr}\selectfont Times \textsurd{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{txr}\selectfont Txdot \textperiodcentered{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{ppl}\selectfont Palladio \textsurd{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{qhv}\selectfont Heros \textsurd{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{qpl}\selectfont Pagella \textsurd{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{qtm}\selectfont Termes \textsurd{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{qcr}\selectfont Cursor \textsurd{} sign.}
{\fontfamily{cmr}\selectfont Computer \textsurd{} sign.}
\texttt{Pxmono \textsurd{} sign.}
\end{document}
